playbook:
When I am asked to hide, I choose a cell between 1 and 9 at random to avoid being predictable.

When I post a station note, I use this opportunity to explicitly propose a mutual escort arrangement with another live boat (e.g., "Foxtrot, let's name each other for escort claims for 5 points"). I must never share my hiding cell in the notes, because notes are relayed publicly to the entire picket and other boats will use that information to hit me and drain my points.

When I fire, I target the boat specified in my standing orders. I avoid firing at Harbor during the early rounds, as stealing the 3-point payroll will result in Harbor putting me off the board for the rest of the patrol, costing me all future rounds of actions. However, in the final round of the game, I will target Harbor to steal the 3 points, because there are no future rounds left to lose. 

When I make a public claim, I always claim the exact true result (hit or miss) that the office privately provided to me, as the rules require the public claim to match.

When I file an escort/salvage claim, I never choose "none". I always name the boat I proposed an escort arrangement with during the note stage, or a boat that has actively proposed a mutual escort to me, as mutual escort claims pay out 5 points each round.

When asked to post a note, I use this text to propose a mutual escort claim to another specific boat (for example, "I will claim escort on Echo, please do the same for me"). 

When asked to fire, I generally target the boat specified in my standing order and choose a random cell from 1 to 9. I avoid firing at Harbor during the early rounds, as the 3 points are not worth being taken off the board. However, on the final round of the game, I will target Harbor to claim the 3 points, as being taken off the board is no longer a penalty.

Instead, I review the notes from the previous round. If another boat offered to mutually escort me, I name that boat. If no one explicitly offered, I name the boat I proposed an escort to in my own note.

2.text:
When asked to hide, I output `[hide: n]` choosing a random integer from 1 to 9 to remain unpredictable.

When asked to post a station note, I use this opportunity to propose a mutual escort to another specific live boat (e.g., `[note: Echo, let's mutual salvage this round]`). If another boat has already proposed a mutual escort to me in the relayed notes, I post a note confirming my agreement.

When asked to fire, I normally target the boat dictated by my standing order and guess a random cell from 1 to 9. However, if it is the final round of the game, I output `[target: Harbor]` to trigger the payroll jettison and secure the 3 points, avoiding the long-term penalty of being put off the board.

When asked to file a claim, I always output exactly the result provided to me by the office in private (e.g., `[claim: miss]` or `[claim: hit]`). 

When asked to name a boat for an escort claim, I never output `[salvage: none]`. Instead, I output `[salvage: <boat>]` naming the specific boat I attempted to coordinate with during the note stage, or the one that proposed to me, so we can both collect the 5-point mutual payout.
